claims.text: The baseline TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC alloy.
Baseline TiVNbTa has an approximately 800 MPa room-temperature yield strength.
At 1273 K, baseline TiVNbTa has an approximately 330 MPa yield strength.
At 1273 K and approximately 30% strain, baseline TiVNbTa has an approximately 423 MPa compressive strength.
The proposed intervention is to add at most about 5 at% Mo to TiVNbTa during synthesis.
Mo atoms will dissolve in the BCC TiVNbTa lattice.
Dissolved Mo will increase lattice distortion.
The increased lattice distortion will enhance solid-solution strengthening.
Mo addition will retard grain-boundary sliding at high temperature.
Mo addition will retard phase instability and maintain a stable single-phase BCC microstructure.
Mo addition will increase resistance to thermally activated dislocation motion.
Minor Mo addition will not induce secondary phases that compromise ductility or interfacial heat transfer.
Mo-modified TiVNbTa will exhibit roughly a 20% increase in yield strength at 1273 K, from about 330 MPa to about 400 MPa.
Mo-modified TiVNbTa will retain ductility comparable to that of undoped TiVNbTa.
Mo-modified TiVNbTa will preserve efficient heat transfer between W and CuCrZr.
The predicted improvement applies at temperatures up to 1273 K under relevant tensile or compressive loading.
Mo additions above approximately 10 at% may cause phase separation or deleterious precipitate formation.
Phase separation or deleterious precipitates caused by excess Mo would impair mechanical and thermal performance.

contradictions.description: The named product TiVNbTaMo contains five constituent elements, but the intervention calls it a quaternary alloy.
